questions.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{16}xy,\, & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 4, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the covariance between $X$ and $Y.$
questions.worked_solution:
The joint support of $X$ and $Y$ is given by the rectangle 

$$
S=[0,2]\times [0,4].
$$

Moreover, we can write 

$$
f(x,y)=g(x)\cdot h(y),
$$

where $g(x)=\frac{x}{2}$ and $h(y)=\frac{y}{8}.$ 

Therefore, $X$ and $Y$ are independent, and consequently $\text{Cov}[X,Y]=0.$

questions.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ |

If $\text{E}[X]=0.8$ and $\text{E}[Y]=2.2,$ calculate the covariance between $X$ and $Y.$
questions.worked_solution:
The covariance of $X$ and $Y$ can be calculated using the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

We use the rule of the lazy statistician to find $\text{E}[XY]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}xy\cdot f(x,y) \\  & =(0)(1)(0.1)+(0)(2)(0.2)+(0)(3)(0.3) \\  & +(2)(1)(0.1)+(2)(2)(0.2)+(2)(3)(0.1) \\  & =1.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the covariance formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =1.6-(0.8)(2.2) \\  & =-0.16.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.11$ | $0.44$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.09$ | $0.36$ |

Calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$

*Hint: It can be shown that $P(X=x,Y=y)=P(X=x)\cdot P(Y=y)$ for all possible values of $x$ and $y.$*
questions.worked_solution:
The covariance of two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint support $S$ is defined as

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y).
$$

We're told that

$$
P(X=x,Y=y)=P(X=x)\cdot P(Y=y)
$$

for all possible values of $x$ and $y.$ Therefore, $X$ and $Y$ are independent. 

Since $X$ are $Y$ are independent, we have $\text{Cov}(X,Y)=0.$

questions.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.6$ | $0$ |

Calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$
questions.worked_solution:
The covariance of two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint support $S$ is defined as

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y).
$$

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y.$ These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ | $0.4$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.6$ | $0$ | $0.6$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.85$ | $0.15$ | $1$ |

We now compute $\text{E}[X]$ and $\text{E}[Y],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & =0\cdot 0.4+2\cdot 0.6 \\  & =0+1.2 \\  & =1.2 \\ \text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =0\cdot 0.85+1\cdot 0.15 \\  & =0+0.15 \\  & =0.15\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for the covariance, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y) \\  & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-1.2)(y-0.15)f(x,y) \\  & =(0-1.2)(0-0.15)f(0,0) \\  & +(0-1.2)(1-0.15)f(0,1) \\  & +(2-1.2)(0-0.15)f(2,0) \\  & +(2-1.2)(1-0.15)f(2,1) \\  & =(-1.2)(-0.15)(0.25) \\  & +(-1.2)(0.85)(0.15) \\  & +(0.8)(-0.15)(0.6) \\  & +(0.8)(0.85)(0) \\  & =-0.18.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: If $\text{E}[X]=5.5,$ $\text{E}[Y]=4.38,$ and $\text{E}[XY]=24.12$ for two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$
questions.worked_solution:
The covariance of $X$ and $Y$ can be calculated using the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

Substituting the given values, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =24.12-(5.5)\cdot (4.38) \\  & =0.03.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance of $X$ and $Y$ is $0.03.$
